sections.heading: 1. The Circulatory System
points: Transport of substances in animals is done by the **circulatory system**: **heart + blood + blood vessels**.
**Blood** carries digested food, oxygen and wastes; its red colour is due to **haemoglobin** in **red blood cells (RBCs)**, which carries **oxygen**.
Blood also has **white blood cells (WBCs)** (fight infection) and **platelets** (help clotting), in a fluid called **plasma**.

sections.heading: 2. Heart and Blood Vessels
points: The **heart** is a muscular pump with **four chambers**; it beats continuously (**heartbeat** ≈ **72 times/minute** at rest); a **pulse** is felt where an artery is near the skin.
**Arteries** carry blood **away from the heart** (thick walls, high pressure; usually oxygen-rich).
**Veins** carry blood **towards the heart** (have valves; usually oxygen-poor).
**Capillaries** = tiny vessels where exchange of materials occurs.

sections.heading: 3. Excretion in Animals
points: **Excretion** = removal of **waste** produced in cells.
In humans, the **kidneys** filter waste (like **urea**) from blood to form **urine**.
Path: **kidneys → ureters → urinary bladder → urethra**.
**Sweat** (from skin) removes water and salts; some animals excrete differently (fish → ammonia; birds/reptiles → uric acid).

sections.heading: 4. Transport in Plants
points: Plants have two transport tissues (**vascular tissue**):

sub: **Xylem** — carries **water and minerals** from **roots upward** to the leaves.
**Phloem** — carries **food (made in leaves)** to all parts of the plant.

points: **Transpiration** = loss of water as vapour from leaves (through stomata); it helps **pull water up** and **cools** the plant.
Root hairs absorb water; water rises due to **root pressure + transpiration pull**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Circulatory system = heart + blood + vessels; haemoglobin (in RBCs) carries oxygen.
Arteries = away from heart (thick, high pressure); veins = towards heart (valves).
Heartbeat ≈ 72/min; pulse = artery beat.
Excretion: kidneys → ureters → bladder → urethra; waste = urea in urine.
Plants: xylem carries water/minerals up; phloem carries food; transpiration = water loss from leaves.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Xylem = water up; phloem = food** — don't swap.
**Arteries carry blood AWAY** from the heart; **veins TOWARDS** it (veins have valves).
**Haemoglobin** (in RBCs) carries **oxygen** and gives blood its red colour.
**Transpiration** = loss of water **vapour** from leaves (helps pull water up).
